messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — gpu-pool=hot-gpu-1 queue_length=18432, sustained >5m, api_errors for /v1/generate up 6x. Autoscaler reporting scale_up failures. Paging oncall: @alice.m :rotating_light:

alice.m: Acked. Jumping in. TLDR: clients seeing 500s + latency spikes?

carla.s: Yep, 5xx rate from frontend spikes at ~18:20 UTC, client retries stacking. Noticed a cascade: driver Xid errors then node flaps.

alice.m: Looking at metrics now. Prometheus: `sum(gpu_queue_length{pool=\"hot-gpu-1\"}) by (pool)` -> 18432. autoscaler_up_errors{reason!~\"\"} shows repeated `driver-attach-failed` and `oom-kernel` errors.

alice.m: grabbing runtime logs from one affected node:
```
[2026-03-14T18:18:45Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID 10203, GPU 0
[2026-03-14T18:18:45Z] runtime: ERROR: failed to init driver: cuda driver lost during init
[2026-03-14T18:18:46Z] kubelet: Evicting pod redwood-runtime-abc-123 due to OOM_killer
```

ben.k: those Xid 13s point to GPU driver/kernel faults, not just memory OOM. We've seen similar after the last driver rollout. When did hot-gpu-1 last receive driver updates?

dylan.p: Driver rollout window ended 2026-03-14 16:30 UTC. Host kernel is 5.15. Driver package build 4.2.7-rc. We had partial rollouts across zones.

alice.m: Autoscaler logs show repeated failures to attach new instances: `attach_device: cudaInit failed: Xid 13`. So autoscaler spins, hits scale limits then gives up -> queue piles up.

carla.s: Customer impact: elevated 95th latency across hosted generate endpoints, some requests return 502/500. CS reporting multiple customer complaints for inference timeouts.

alice.m: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Stop new jobs hitting hot-gpu-1 by updating routing -> move to fallback pool (warm-gpu). 2) Pause autoscaler for hot-gpu-1 to avoid churn. 3) Drain and cordon affected nodes to force replacement on healthy driver variant. 4) Roll back driver package on hot-gpu-1 nodes to previous stable (4.2.5). 5) If rollback not fast enough, enable model-fallback policy (route large models to lower-capacity variant) to reduce queue.

ben.k: I'll do the routing change. Patching LB rule to exclude pool hot-gpu-1 and route to warm-gpu with overflow weights. Command: `./infractl route-set --from pool:hot-gpu-1 --to pool:warm-gpu --weight 0 --reason \"incident 4112223334\"`

infra-bot: deploy queued: route-change-job-4112223334 (dry-run) -> applying...

deploy-bot: route-change-job-4112223334: SUCCESS (applied in 2 regions).

alice.m: Routing change is live. Queue length on hot-gpu-1 remains high but ingest reduced. warm-gpu shows increased load but within capacity for now.

carla.s: Autoscaler paused on hot-gpu-1: `autoscaler pause --pool hot-gpu-1 --reason incident-4112223334`. Done.

dylan.p: Starting node cordon/drain for nodes reporting Xid errors. Using kops/gke: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-77 && kubectl drain node/gpu-node-77 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

alice.m: Drain started. Observed flaky nodes frequently re-registering then failing healthchecks (nodename gpu-node-77, gpu-node-82). Suggest replacement with nodes that have driver 4.2.5.

ben.k: I can trigger a targeted reimage job to the 4.2.5 image for the pool. Command: `infractl node-reimage --pool hot-gpu-1 --image driver-4.2.5 --parallel 3`

dylan.p: Reimage job submitted. We'll backfill capacity from warm-gpu while that runs. Need to monitor preemption/eviction rates.

carla.s: Quick check: Are any Dedicated customers pinned to hot-gpu-1? If so we need to flag SLA impact.

alice.m: Querying: `select count(distinct customer_id) from allocations where pool='hot-gpu-1' and type='dedicated'` -> 2 customers (acct-743, acct-998). Notifying AE for those accounts. *@ben.k please cc support ops.*

ben.k: Noted. Messaging AE and support now.

infra-bot: reimage-job-4112223334: started node/gpu-node-77, node/gpu-node-82, node/gpu-node-85

alice.m: While reimages roll, enable conservative throttling for anonymous/unknown API keys to buy headroom. Patch rate-limiter: `rlsctl set --policy protect-critical --anon-qps 0.2`

carla.s: Applied throttling. 95th latency across generate down ~30% after routing+throttle. Errors still > baseline but trending down.

dylan.p: Reimage progress: node-77 healthy on 4.2.5, node-82 failed post-boot selftest (kernel panic), node-85 healthy. Requeued node-82 for manual inspection.

alice.m: Good. Next: confirm autoscaler safe to resume once pool nodes are mostly healthy (>=80% healthy). We'll keep autoscaler paused until then.

ben.k: From a deployment perspective, we should prevent the 4.2.7 rollout from resuming. Lock the driver rollout job: `deployctl lock driver-rollout --tag 4.2.7 --reason incident-4112223334`

deploy-bot: Lock applied for driver-tag 4.2.7 by ben.k.

carla.s: Noting customer impact: CS tickets created for acct-743/acct-998; status updated to \"investigating\".

alice.m: Prep for handoff: I'm oncall for another 30m. Ben, can you take rel-eng escalation and follow reimage until stable? Dylan to verify node health and kernel logs. Carla continue CS comms.

ben.k: Taking lead after 30m. I'll be oncall handoff. My pager is on.

dylan.p: I'll keep watch on the node selftest logs and follow-up on node-82 kernel panic. Will collect dmesg + nvml logs and open an infra ticket if hardware suspected.

alice.m: Quick summary to paste in postmortem: root cause appears to be new driver 4.2.7 causing intermittent Xid 13 GPU faults under our workload, which prevented autoscaler from successfully attaching GPUs causing scale-up churn and queue growth -> increased user latencies and errors. Immediate mitigations: routing change, autoscaler pause, targeted reimage to driver 4.2.5, throttling, and driver-rollout lock. Next steps: full rollback audit, reproduce in staging, hardware triage for node-82, contact driver vendor with logs.

carla.s: Adding action item: create eval harness test to run our stress prompt set against 4.2.7 under load. Assign to eng-ml.

alice.m: Handing off to ben.k in 30m. Moving thread to \"oncall-handoff\". If anything spikes, @ben.k and @dylan.p are primary. I'm marking incident active and will open a pager duty incident ticket with links. :white_check_mark:

ben.k: Acknowledged. Will post follow-up when pool healthy and autoscaler resumed.

incident-bot: Incident 4112223334 status=active, created_by=incident-bot, severity=P1, owner=alice.m, linked_ticket=PD-4112223334

alice.m: Leaving notes: logs snapshot uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/4112223334/logs.tar.gz. Added checklist to PD ticket. Good work team.

ben.k: Thanks all — will follow through on reimage progress and resumption plan.

dylan.p: I'll attach kernel/dmesg logs for node-82 to the ticket and schedule hardware review.

carla.s: CS will continue outbound comms for impacted customers, update when we resume autoscaler.

alice.m: Handoff complete.
